summary.text: Seth Magaziner is the Democratic incumbent seeking a third term in Rhode Island's 2nd District. A Bristol native, he worked as a teacher and in investment management before serving as Rhode Island's General Treasurer from 2015 to 2023, and he was first elected to the U.S. House in 2022. His official biography describes his work as focused on lowering drug prices, protecting Social Security and Medicare, and abortion rights.

paragraphs.text: Magaziner was born July 22, 1983, in Bristol, Rhode Island, where, according to his official House biography, he grew up.
He earned a bachelor's degree in history from Brown University in 2006 and an MBA from the Yale School of Management in 2010.
From 2006 to 2008 he taught elementary school in Opelousas, Louisiana, as a Teach For America member; Ballotpedia lists his employer as the St. Landry Parish School Board.
After business school he worked as a vice president at Trillium Asset Management; earlier, in 2009, he was an associate at the Rhode Island venture capital firm Point Judith Capital.

Magaziner won the 2014 Democratic primary for General Treasurer over former treasurer Frank Caprio, then won the general election and served from January 2015 to January 2023, succeeding Gina Raimondo.
His official biography says that as Treasurer he led an initiative to rebuild school buildings across the state and created programs to invest in clean energy projects.
Magaziner announced a run for governor in September 2021, withdrew in January 2022 after Rep. James Langevin announced his retirement, and ran for the 2nd District seat instead.
He won the September 2022 Democratic primary with 54% of the vote and the November 2022 general election over Republican Allan Fung, 50% to 47%.
He was re-elected in 2024 with 58% of the vote over Republican Steve Corvi and ran unopposed in the September 9, 2026 Democratic primary.

In the 119th Congress Magaziner serves on the House Natural Resources Committee and the Committee on Homeland Security, where he is ranking member of the Subcommittee on Counterterrorism and Intelligence.
According to his official biography, he and his wife, Julia, have two children, and he has served on the boards of Crossroads Rhode Island and, previously, Common Cause Rhode Island.
